base64_credential_padding_cases._comment: is_base64_credential requires canonical padding on every supported Python. 3.10's b64decode(validate=True) accepts excess padding that 3.11+ rejects; the result must not depend on the interpreter.

query_credential_cases._comment: find_query_credential(segment) over one raw URL query segment. prefix is the verbatim text kept ahead of the credential; credential is the base64(user:pass) as the client produced it. The space_for_plus row is the shape URLSearchParams hands Playwright's queryString array: '+' decoded to a space.

mac_regex_cases._comment: MAC_RE over free text: matches are the MAC substrings found, in order. Six hex pairs joined by ':' or '-' match wherever they occur, glued to anything, so validate and sanitize agree on every such run. Across 11,953 MAC runs in the cable_modem_monitor fleet (2026-09-12) every one sits between punctuation or whitespace. A longer separated run is read six pairs at a time. Bare 12-hex is not matched: without a label it cannot be told from any other hex run.

url_credential_cases._comment: iter_url_credentials(request): every base64(user:pass) credential in a request's query, as find_query_credential reads it: the URL string's segments first, then the queryString array (so a credential recorded in both appears twice). The query is read with split_url_query — from the first '?' to the next '#', so a hash route's '#/page?…' parameters count and a credential in a plain fragment does not — which never raises, unlike urlparse (an unbalanced IPv6 bracket). Malformed requests yield nothing.

json_identity_key_cases._comment: classify_identity_field(key, value): a key that names a serial or MAC, holding a value of that identity's shape. Keys are read as words (camelCase, acronyms, separators); the identity must end the key, though its last word may carry a glued prefix ('cmserialnumber') — except a word starting 'hmac'. A serial placeholder is not a serial; a MAC placeholder is still a MAC (it cannot be told from a real one). Serial values are one whitespace-free token of 5+ characters with a digit (every real serial across the fleet carries one; the digit-free values are placeholders like '-'). MAC values are any MAC form: separated, bare 12-hex, or dotted.

transport_body_cases._comment: decode_transport_body(content): the text a HAR response body carries. A body without 'encoding' is already text. A base64 body is decoded with the mime type's charset — or strict UTF-8 when none is declared or the declared one is unknown or not a text encoding. Bytes that do not decode are binary (None), except under a text mime type (is_text_mime), where undeclared non-UTF-8 bytes are read as latin-1: capture writes such a page base64 when it is not UTF-8, and browsers render undeclared pages in a Latin charset. Text holding NUL is binary.

base64_payload_cases._comment: decode_base64_payload(value): the text of a base64-wrapped structured payload — a JSON object or array, or a URL — whose colon would otherwise read as user:pass. Padding may be missing or excess (URLs strip and miscount it). A JSON scalar, colon text, non-UTF-8 bytes, and anything not base64 are not payloads.

text_mime_cases._comment: mime_kind(mime): what a mime type declares its body to be — markup (HTML, XML, any +xml), json (any json subtype or +json, whatever the type: DM1000's applation/json), text (other text/*, JavaScript, form data), or null when the type says nothing about text. is_text_mime is kind != null. Parameters and case are ignored; a subtype merely containing 'json' or 'xml' is not one.

json_container_cases._comment: parse_json_container(text): a JSON object or array, or null. Scalars, invalid JSON and nesting too deep for the parser are not containers — hostile nesting must not crash either tool. 'nesting' builds '[' * n + ']' * n instead of a literal text.

constant_mac_cases._comment: is_constant_mac(mac): one byte repeated — broadcast, zero — in any layout. Protocol constants, not identities: neither tool treats them as PII.

query_payload_cases._comment: find_query_payload(segment): a base64-wrapped JSON or URL payload in one raw query segment. prefix is kept verbatim; encoded is the base64 with URL transport encoding undone; quoted records that the segment percent-encoded it. Credentials and non-payloads give null.

url_password_cases._comment: split_url_password(url): the password in a URL's userinfo, split so the URL reassembles byte-for-byte. The authority ends at the first '/', '?' or '#'; its userinfo runs to the authority's last '@' (as browsers parse it, so a password or an email-address username may hold '@'); the password starts after the userinfo's first ':'. A port, a path '@', or a user without a password give none.

body_route_cases._comment: route_body(mime, text): the engine a response body's text goes to, with the parsed JSON for the json route. Text that parses as a JSON object or array is JSON whatever its type declares (HNAP answers as text/html); otherwise a markup type goes to the HTML engine, any other text type to the text path, and a type that says nothing about text is sniffed (markup, else text).

mac_placeholder_cases._comment: is_mac_placeholder(value): a value hash_mac could have written — a MAC in any layout whose first octet is 02, hex lowercase. For a value already known to be a MAC (under a MAC-named key); as a free-text test a bare 02-prefixed hex run is ambiguous.

network_value_regex_cases._comment: The shared value regexes both engines (HTML passes 4-6 and 11, and the JSON/text string patterns) and validate use: matches are the substrings found, in order. For ipv6 a candidate counts only when is_ipv6_host_address accepts it, so clock times, MACs and the constants :: and ::1 are not host addresses. pii.json mirrors public_ip, ipv6 and email verbatim for check_for_pii.

credential_value_action_cases._comment: credential_value_action(value): what both tools do with a non-empty, unredacted value a response serves under a credential-named key. The fleet's firmware translation tables hold Yes/No buttons (kept) and prose UI strings (offered for review: a passphrase can hold spaces); anything else is redacted.

cases.value: Basic settings for the admin password

iter_json_strings_cases._comment: iter_json_strings(parsed) yields every decoded string — object keys and string values, in arrays too, shadowed duplicates included — at any depth; numbers, booleans and null are not strings.

set_cookie_attribute_grammar_cases._comment: RFC 6265 Set-Cookie attribute grammar (is_set_cookie_attribute): a segment a user agent would apply as an attribute.

cookie_segment_action_cases._comment: cookie_segment_actions: per ;-segment of a cookie header, keep / value (the pair's value is cookie data) / token (a nameless cookie). One rule for the sanitizer and validate.
